service.description: Extract HotWax OMS orders for an automation window and write normalized JSON output to the automation data-manager folder.

parameter.name: omsRestSourceConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig identifier.

parameter.name: automationExecutionId
parameter.description: Automation execution id used to choose the default data-manager output folder.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted automation owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.

parameter.name: windowStart
parameter.description: Start of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds.

parameter.name: windowEnd
parameter.description: End of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds.

parameter.name: outputLocation
parameter.description: Optional output directory. Defaults to runtime://datamanager/reconciliation-runs/{automationExecutionId}/{timestamp}/.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name. Defaults to oms-orders-{fromMillis}-{thruMillis}.json.

parameter.name: keepRecordFields
parameter.description: Optional projection: top-level record fields to keep in the output file. When present, each order is trimmed to these fields after reconciliation filtering and before writing (callers compute the list from the rule set's join-key and rule fields plus the display fields). Absent means full untrimmed records (backward compatible).

parameter.name: sourceFilters
parameter.description: Optional record-exclusion rules. Each rule names a top-level record field and a comma-separated list of exact values; matching orders are dropped before the extract file is written and counted per rule in requestMetadata.filters.configuredExclusions. Absent or empty means no configured exclusions (backward compatible).

parameter.name: reconciliationRunResultId
parameter.description: Optional observability run id. On its own it is enough for the extractor to heartbeat a running order count onto the run's RUNNING extract step as pages are consumed, so the live view can show the count climbing. Advisory only.

parameter.name: progressStageCode
parameter.description: Which extract stage this run is: EXTRACT_FILE1 or EXTRACT_FILE2. Required for progress to land, because the heartbeat targets the RUNNING step for this stage and the same extractor runs on either side depending on the saved run's source order. Defaults to EXTRACT_FILE2 for callers that predate this parameter.

parameter.name: expectedRecordCount
parameter.description: Optional expected total, which adds a progress percent alongside the count — typically the other side's extracted record count for the same window. Only the second extract of a run can supply one; the first has nothing finished to divide against.

parameter.name: exchangeManifestFileLocation
parameter.description: Location of the exchange-manifest sidecar written when the window contained excluded exchange orders; null otherwise. Identities/amounts only, capped at 500 entries.

service.description: Extract HotWax OMS sales orders at ORDER grain over the GraphQL endpoint (/rest/s1/graphql) instead of /rest/s1/oms/orders. Same parameters, same output document, same exclusions, filters and projection as extract#HotWaxOmsOrders: the REST pipeline runs unchanged over GraphQL pages (OmsGqlOrderPageSource). Adds hasPaymentPreference / paymentMethodTypeIds for the presence OPP rule (DAR-BE-064). A DISTINCT service name is required: the connector registry resolves rows by it.

parameter.name: lookupKeys
parameter.description: DAR-BE-120. Read only these orders by orderId, whatever their date, instead of the window: a conclusion lookup. A caller checks this parameter is declared before sending keys, so a connector without it is never asked for a whole window instead.

parameter.name: lookupKeyField
parameter.description: The record field lookupKeys are values of: orderId, or externalId (the Shopify order id; DAR-BE-156, a Shopify-paired audit check's re-check).

service.description: DAR-BE-157. Every sellable HotWax product (not virtual, FINISHED_GOOD or MARKETING_PKG_PICK, not discontinued) over the GraphQL endpoint, one record per product keyed by nsKey: its NETSUITE_PRODUCT_ID (the NetSuite item internal id), HOTWAX-ONLY:productId when it has none, DUPLICATE:id:productId for every product after the first sharing one. Not windowed: windowStart/windowEnd are accepted and ignored (requestMetadata.windowIgnored). A DISTINCT service name is required: the connector registry resolves rows by it.

Extract HotWax OMS orders for an automation window from the purpose-built /rest/s1/oms/reconciliationOrders endpoint, writing normalized JSON output to the automation data-manager folder. Same in/out contract and same on-disk file shape as extract#HotWaxOmsOrders, so the automation edge and the Spark compare stage are unchanged; the endpoint differs in that it filters to comparison-eligible sales orders server-side, projects to a fixed field set, honours pageSize, and reports hasMore/ordersCount instead of leaving termination to be inferred.
A distinct service name from extract#HotWaxOmsOrders is required because the connector registry resolves a connector row by its extract service name. Adoption is opt-in: a rule set moves to this connector by pointing its source at sourceConfigType HOTWAX_OMS_REST_RECON, against the same HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig row.
GATING: the endpoint returns a fixed field set, so before enabling this connector for a rule set, verify that rule set's join key and every field-comparison field fall inside {orderId, externalId, orderName, grandTotal, orderDate, statusId}. A rule set needing any other field must stay on extract#HotWaxOmsOrders.

parameter.name: omsRestSourceConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig identifier. Reuses the same OMS credentials and baseUrl as sales-order extraction; only the path differs, and the path is fixed by the extractor rather than read from the config's ordersPath.

parameter.name: windowStart
parameter.description: Start of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds. Sent as the half-open lower bound orderDateFrom.

parameter.name: windowEnd
parameter.description: End of the automation window, same accepted formats as windowStart. Sent as orderDateThru, which the endpoint treats as EXCLUSIVE — an order timestamped exactly at the bound belongs to the next window, so consecutive chunks do not double-count their boundary.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name. Defaults to oms-orders-{fromMillis}-{thruMillis}.json, matching the legacy extractor so saved-run file-side matching is unaffected.

parameter.name: keepRecordFields
parameter.description: Optional projection: top-level record fields to keep in the output file. Normally a no-op here because the endpoint already projects server-side; retained so the parameter contract matches extract#HotWaxOmsOrders and so a caller asking for a narrower set than the endpoint's still gets it.

parameter.name: sourceFilters
parameter.description: Optional record-exclusion rules, same semantics as extract#HotWaxOmsOrders. These stay client-side on this connector too: the endpoint has no knowledge of tenant exclusion rules, so matching runs in the extractor before output.

parameter.name: reconciliationRunResultId
parameter.description: Optional observability run id for progress heartbeats. Advisory only.

parameter.name: progressStageCode
parameter.description: Which extract stage this run is: EXTRACT_FILE1 or EXTRACT_FILE2. Defaults to EXTRACT_FILE2.

parameter.name: expectedRecordCount
parameter.description: Optional expected total, which adds a progress percent alongside the count.

parameter.name: exchangeManifestFileLocation
parameter.description: Location of the exchange-manifest sidecar written when the window contained exchange orders; null otherwise. Same shape and same 500-entry cap as the legacy extractor, but built from the endpoint's inline originalOrderId / originalExternalId fields, so it costs no pair-lookup round-trips.

service.description:
Extract HotWax OMS returns for an automation window from /rest/s1/oms/reconciliationReturns, writing normalized JSON output to the automation data-manager folder (DAR-BE-018).
New capability — Darpan did not reconcile returns before this service, so there is no legacy path to preserve. Same {records, metadata} on-disk contract and the same automation-edge in/out parameters as the orders extractors, so the automation executor, progress heartbeat and Spark compare stage are unchanged.
Lines arrive nested inside their header as items[] and are written through nested (RQ-21); do not flatten. The endpoint pre-excludes returns with no Shopify reference server-side and reports that as excludedNoShopifyRefCount; tenant-configured exclusions (typically on returnChannelEnumId) still run client-side here, on the population that survives.

parameter.name: omsRestSourceConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig identifier. Reuses the same OMS credentials and baseUrl as order extraction; the returns path is pinned by the extractor.

parameter.name: automationExecutionId
parameter.description: Automation execution id used to choose the default data-manager output folder.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted automation owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.

parameter.name: windowStart
parameter.description: Start of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds. Sent as the half-open lower bound returnDateFrom, which filters on ReturnHeader.entryDate (RQ-22).

parameter.name: windowEnd
parameter.description: End of the automation window, same accepted formats. Sent as returnDateThru, which the endpoint treats as EXCLUSIVE, so consecutive chunks do not double-count their boundary.

parameter.name: outputLocation
parameter.description: Optional output directory. Defaults to runtime://datamanager/reconciliation-runs/{automationExecutionId}/{timestamp}/.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name. Defaults to oms-returns-{fromMillis}-{thruMillis}.json.

parameter.name: keepRecordFields
parameter.description: Optional projection of top-level record fields. items[] is always retained regardless of this list, because the nested-line contract (RQ-21) does not survive a projection that names only header fields.

parameter.name: sourceFilters
parameter.description: Optional record-exclusion rules, same semantics as the order extractors. These run client-side: the endpoint has no knowledge of tenant exclusion rules. The expected rule here excludes returns whose returnChannelEnumId never has a Shopify counterpart.

parameter.name: reconciliationRunResultId
parameter.description: Optional observability run id for progress heartbeats. Advisory only.

parameter.name: progressStageCode
parameter.description: Which extract stage this run is: EXTRACT_FILE1 or EXTRACT_FILE2. Defaults to EXTRACT_FILE2.

parameter.name: expectedRecordCount
parameter.description: Optional expected total, which adds a progress percent alongside the count.

service.description:
Extract HotWax OMS returns for an automation window over the OMS GraphQL API (connector OMS_RETURNS_GQL, DAR-BE-040 fix 3), writing the same {records, metadata} file as extract#HotWaxOmsReturns.
Why it exists: /rest/s1/oms/reconciliationReturns serves REFUNDED returns only. Live on gorjana 2026-10-03 it returned none of the 268 RETURN_REQUESTED returns since Oct 1, so every pending return Shopify reported read as missing in HotWax. GraphQL `returns` carries them.
Records are built to the REST record exactly — 110 settled returns matched REST on every field, items included (tools/live-probes/OmsReturnsGqlParityProbe) — so a rule set moves between the two connectors with no rule change. Like REST it excludes returns with no Shopify reference (counted as excludedNoShopifyRefCount) and, by default, RETURN_CANCELLED (excludedCancelledCount), which the Shopify side suppresses (DAR-BE-027). Needs the OMS GraphQL upgrade (gorjana 2026-09-30); on an OMS without it the extract FAILS rather than returning an empty file.

parameter.name: lookupKeys
parameter.description: DAR-BE-119. Read only these records by key (returnId), whatever their date, instead of the window: an audit re-checking its older open findings. A caller checks this parameter is declared before sending keys, so a connector without it is never asked for a whole window instead.

parameter.name: lookupKeyField
parameter.description: The record field lookupKeys are values of: returnId.

parameter.name: windowStart
parameter.description: Start of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds. Sent as the half-open lower bound on entryDate.

parameter.name: windowEnd
parameter.description: End of the automation window, same accepted formats. Exclusive upper bound on entryDate, so consecutive chunks do not double-count their boundary.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name. Defaults to oms-returns-{fromMillis}-{thruMillis}.json, the REST extract's name, because the file is the same contract.

parameter.name: sourceFilters
parameter.description: Optional record-exclusion rules, same semantics as the order extractors. These run client-side, after the built-in exclusions. The expected rule here excludes returns whose returnChannelEnumId never has a Shopify counterpart.

parameter.name: includeReturnsWithoutShopifyRef
parameter.description: DAR-BE-094. Keep the returns with no Shopify reference (counted as keptNoShopifyRefCount) instead of excluding them: the OMS's own Happiness Guarantee and sellable returns, which Shopify never sees but NetSuite must. For a check against NetSuite (R8), set in the automation source's safeMetadataJson.parameters; every Shopify comparison leaves it off.

parameter.name: onlyCancelledReturns
parameter.description: DAR-BE-094 R16. Read ONLY the returns the OMS cancelled (asked of the OMS by status), with or without a Shopify reference: for a check that nothing stays open in NetSuite for them. Set in the automation source's safeMetadataJson.parameters.

service.description:
Extract HotWax OMS order lines as ONE RECORD PER UNIT for the DAR-BE-050 Shopify-to-OMS unit presence pair, writing normalized JSON output to the automation data-manager folder. Served by the same /rest/s1/oms/orders endpoint as sales orders; the grain, not the endpoint, is what differs. A distinct service name from extract#HotWaxOmsOrders is required because the connector registry resolves a connector row by its extract service name.
WHY UNITS AND NOT LINES: OMS explodes a Shopify line of quantity N into N single-unit OrderItems for routing, and the Spark compare core is a left_anti join followed by .distinct() - set semantics. At line grain a line OMS imported SHORT still matches a complete Shopify line, so the pair reports clean on exactly the defect it exists to find. Each record therefore carries a unitOrdinal, and the compare key is (shopifyOrderId, shopifyLineId, unitOrdinal).
NO keepRecordFields: the unit record IS the projection. Passing an order-shaped field list would strip every field a unit record has and still report a successful extract.
THE EXCHANGE EXCLUSION IS KEPT, NOT INVERTED, and this is the thing most likely to be "fixed" wrongly. It looks like an order-grain artefact - two OMS orders colliding on one compare_id - and therefore looks safe to drop at item grain. Measured against gorjana production: an OMS EXC- order's externalId names the ORIGINAL Shopify order (15 of 15 resolved), and Shopify adds the exchange line to that original's lineItems (12 of 12, by set difference). That original may be months old, so a creation-windowed Shopify sweep never includes it while OMS lands a new EXC- order inside the window. Inverting the exclusion makes every exchange a false missing-in-Shopify, roughly 1 order in 9. Exchange-line presence is a separate pair (DAR-BE-004).

parameter.description: Tenant-owned HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig identifier. Unit extraction reuses the same OMS credentials and baseUrl as sales-order extraction.

parameter.description: Trusted automation owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.

parameter.description: OrderHeader date field the window filters on. Defaults to orderDate, which is what the Shopify side's created_at window matches. Changing one side only produces the DAR-BE-038 skew: structurally guaranteed false positives on every run.

parameter.name: orderStatusIds
parameter.description: Optional statuses to include, sent to the OMS as a server-side IN filter.

parameter.name: outputLocation
parameter.description: Optional output directory. Defaults to runtime://datamanager/reconciliation-runs/{automationExecutionId}/{timestamp}/.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name.

parameter.name: sourceFilters

parameter.name: reconciliationRunResultId

parameter.name: progressStageCode

service.description:
Tri-system order runs (spec 2026-09-30, D4). Extract HotWax OMS order items as ONE RECORD PER UNIT for the OMS-to-NetSuite hops, writing normalized JSON output to the automation data-manager folder. Same /rest/s1/oms/orders endpoint and the same flattener as extract#HotWaxOmsOrderLineUnits; a distinct service name is required because the connector registry resolves a connector row by its extract service name, and this one is gated on the OMS_ORDER_ITEMS endpoint.
Each unit carries unitState (OPEN, COMPLETED, CANCELLED, OTHER) and stateOrdinal (1..k within order, line and state), netsuiteOrderId (the NETSUITE_ORDER_ID identification, or the literal NONE, because composite keys refuse a blank part), omsOrderStatusId and the ship group's facilityId.
TWO DELIBERATE DIFFERENCES from extract#HotWaxOmsOrderLineUnits, which is why this is a connector and not a filter (changing that service's defaults would change a shipped pair): the exchange exclusion is OFF, because an EXC- order is a real OMS order that syncs to NetSuite the same day and the exclusion exists only for Shopify's creation-window asymmetry; and items with no Shopify order or line id are KEPT with that id null (counted as keptNullShopifyIdCount), because the NetSuite hops key on the OMS order.
Source filters run per UNIT (D3), against the order's top-level fields overlaid by the unit row, so unitState and item statusId can be filtered on.

parameter.name: omsRestSourceConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig identifier. Item extraction reuses the same OMS credentials and baseUrl as sales-order extraction.

parameter.name: windowFieldName
parameter.description: OrderHeader date field the window filters on. Defaults to orderDate. Changing one side of a pair only produces the DAR-BE-038 skew: structurally guaranteed false positives on every run.

parameter.name: sourceFilters
parameter.description: Optional include/exclude rules, same operators as extract#HotWaxOmsOrders, evaluated per UNIT against the order's top-level fields overlaid by the unit row (the unit wins on a shared name such as statusId). Per-rule counts are units.

parameter.name: requestMetadata
parameter.description: Carries keptNullShopifyIdCount (items emitted with a null Shopify id), droppedNullLineIdCount (structurally zero here) and nonUnitQuantityCount beside the usual filter counts.

service.description:
DAR-BE-116. extract#HotWaxOmsOrderItems over GraphQL (every OMS read goes through GraphQL): the same ONE RECORD PER UNIT, the same flattener, the same two deliberate differences from the Shopify-side line units (exchange exclusion OFF, items without a Shopify id KEPT). Orders are read with their ship groups, the items by orderId in batches, each placed under its ship group; a multi-day window runs as parallel day slices on the endpoint's one cost bucket. A distinct service name because the connector registry resolves a connector row by its extract service name; this one is gated on the OMS_ORDER_ITEMS_GQL endpoint.
NOT carried: salesChannelEnumId, which gorjana's GraphQL Order type does not have (SDL 2026-10-23). A source filter on it is refused rather than ignored, so a run that concludes on the sales channel stays on extract#HotWaxOmsOrderItems.

parameter.name: lookupKeys
parameter.description: DAR-BE-119. Read only these records by key (omsOrderId (the OMS orderId)), whatever their date, instead of the window: an audit re-checking its older open findings. A caller checks this parameter is declared before sending keys, so a connector without it is never asked for a whole window instead.

parameter.name: lookupKeyField
parameter.description: The record field lookupKeys are values of: omsOrderId (the OMS orderId).

parameter.name: omsRestSourceConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig identifier; the same credential and baseUrl answer /rest/s1/graphql.

parameter.name: windowFieldName
parameter.description: Only orderDate (or empty): the GraphQL order extract windows on orderDate and refuses any other field rather than widening the extract.

parameter.name: sourceFilters
parameter.description: Optional include/exclude rules evaluated per UNIT, as on extract#HotWaxOmsOrderItems. A rule on a field the GraphQL unit does not carry (salesChannelEnumId) fails the extract.

parameter.name: requestMetadata
parameter.description: As extract#HotWaxOmsOrderItems: keptNullShopifyIdCount, droppedNullLineIdCount and nonUnitQuantityCount beside the usual filter counts, plus the GraphQL pagination (sliceCount, pageCount, lookupCalls).

service.description:
Point-existence check for OMS return ids against the reconciliation returns endpoint, the missing-in-OMS mirror of Shopify's lookup#ShopifyRefundOrReturnIds. The saved-run verification pass calls this to confirm or refute "missing in OMS" differences.
Escapes the run window by construction: OMS windows on entryDate (when a return was CREATED) while the Shopify side windows on the event createdAt (when it was REFUNDED), so a return opened weeks before its refund sits inside one window and far outside the other. Measured 2026-08-20, that mismatch explained 45 of 59 remaining differences, median age 11 days.
The endpoint honours a CSV externalId filter, so ids are checked in batches, and every returned record is echo-checked against the ids actually requested — a sibling filter (orderExternalId) was proven to be silently ignored while still answering HTTP 200 with an unfiltered corpus. A failed lookup returns ok=false with both id lists empty — it never classifies an id as missing.
Ids neither REST pass resolves get a GraphQL returnIdentifications(idValue:) pass (DAR-BE-040): the REST endpoint serves refunded returns only, so a pending return is invisible to it. Ids the GraphQL pass cannot check come back in unresolvedIds — unchecked, never confirmed missing.

parameter.name: omsRestSourceConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned HotWaxOmsRestSourceConfig identifier.

parameter.name: externalIds
parameter.description: Shopify refund or return ids as they appear in the OMS externalId field.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted run owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.
